exposure: timing of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) diagnosis and management (early second-trimester vs. third-trimester)
management approaches for early second-trimester PAS (induction abortion, gravid hysterectomy, dilation and evacuation, hysterotomy alone)
outcome: maternal morbidity (hemorrhage/blood transfusion, shock/coagulopathy, hospitalization duration)
cohort: The study included 905 cases of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) diagnosed between 14 and 22 weeks of gestation and managed in-hospital, compared to 5365 cases of PAS managed with cesarean hysterectomy between 34 and 36 weeks of gestation.
finding: Morbidity associated with early second-trimester Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) was substantial regardless of the management approach, with early second-trimester gravid hysterectomy showing higher rates of hemorrhage, shock, and prolonged hospitalization compared to third-trimester cesarean hysterectomy.
gest_age: Between 14 and 22 weeks of gestation for early PAS cases, and between 34 and 36 weeks of gestation for third-trimester PAS comparison cases.
